Endothelin-1 (ET-1) has been found to play a role in aggravating the development of acute hemorrhagic pancreatitis. Studies have suggested that altered ET-1 levels may be involved in the pathogenesis of rebound hypertension and hypotension during hemodialysis, as well as its involvement in inflammation during ERCP-induced pancreatitis.

Regarding the question about whether endothelin-1 is a biomarker for acute pancreatitis, the correct answer is: yes, serum pancreatic lipase is a more accurate biomarker than serum amylase. This is because lipase levels are directly related to pancreatic function and can be affected by pancreatitis, whereas amylase levels may not accurately reflect pancreatic damage.

To summarize, endothelin-1 has been found to play a role in aggravating acute hemorrhagic pancreatitis, and its levels may be elevated during hemodialysis. Additionally, lipase levels are a more accurate biomarker for acute pancreatitis than amylase.
